parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Mongol ᠠᠪᠤᠷᠠᠬᠤ (aburaqu, “to save, rescue, help”). Cognate with Chuvash упра (upra, “to protect, guard”) and Yakut абраа (abraa).
Learned borrowing from Middle Mongol ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ (belge, “official seal, stamp”), itself from Proto-Turkic *bẹlgü (“sign, mark”). Borrowed into modern Turkish during the Language reform. Doublet of belgi.
From Ottoman Turkish قراول (karavul), قرهغول (karağol), reinterpreted as the compound of kara (“black”) + kol (“arm”). Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯ (qaraɣul).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نوكر (nöker), from Middle Mongol ᠨᠥᠬᠦᠷ (ṅwykwr /⁠nökör⁠/).

parole.testo: Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠵᠠᠰᠠᠭ (ǰasaɣ). Doublet of yasak.

Learned borrowing from Ottoman Turkish یاسامق (yasamaq), from Middle Mongol ᠵᠠᠰᠠᠬᠤ (ǰasaqu). Cognate to Chagatai یاساماق (yʾsʾmʾq /⁠yasamaq⁠/), Kazakh жасау (jasaw), Uyghur ياسىماق (yasimaq). Reintroduced to the language in 1935.
